review_type: Repository-owner-commissioned AI-assisted Econometrica numerical-methods advisory review
recommendation: Reject in the present form and do not continue the cumulative manuscript through another ordinary revision round. A new, sharply focused paper on from-primitives neural Bellman training and direct certification in compact nonlinear control could merit evaluation, but the R42 evidence does not establish an Econometrica-level method-specific contribution for the broad NBO program.

reviewed_science_snapshot.status: Completed source-bound science revision; no rematerialized R42 main article, supplement, response or PDF exists on the reviewed branch.

retained_first_run.correction: Algebraically equivalent stable inverse-softplus; economic primitives, seeds, targets, training budgets and comparison methods unchanged.

blocking_findings: R42 is a source-and-evidence revision, not a materialized paper revision; the authoritative article remains R41 and does not contain the new results.
The scalar direct-neural method reaches the tighter 0.04 all-state target in only six of twelve services, while spline reaches both targets in all twelve.
Every matched scalar spline global certificate is tighter, and the signed displayed-state direct comparisons never favor neural.
The flexible coupled ridge comparator is more reliable, faster at the 0.25 target in all six services, and has the tighter final gap in four of six.
The coupled study lacks direct neural-minus-ridge policy-value intervals; separate regret bounds do not rank actual policy costs.
The nonlinear experiments remain one- and two-dimensional tensor-cover constructions rather than a scaling result.
No stable matched work-to-certified-accuracy advantage is established; scalar and coupled timings are single descriptive runs and conventional methods are often faster.
Adaptive precision certifies but is slower in 26 of 36 paired runs and approximately 0.98 percent slower in aggregate than fixed64.
Three fixed seeds and a finite catalogue do not establish nonlinear optimizer reliability or a method-level training distribution.
The broad cumulative manuscript and applications remain disproportionate to the compact nonlinear training-to-certificate result established by R42.
positive_findings: R42 executes fresh own-future neural training from economic primitives rather than certifying inherited frozen networks.
The scalar neural services use no conventional labels, inherited weights or spline fallback.
The service boundary includes target generation, fitting, failed refinements, policy extraction, verification and durable output.
The coupled experiment uses trainable hidden features, continuous simplex actions and continuous innovations with an all-state certificate.
A flexible 96-feature ridge comparator is added rather than interpreting quadratic failure as neural superiority.
The precision catalogue contains three repetitions and preserves all rejected low-precision proposals.
The failed first run and stable numerical correction are explicitly retained and identified.
Provenance, record hashing, source hashing and failure preservation are exceptionally strong.

review_manifest.json.description: Pinned review scope, evidence identities, findings, limitations and change policy; deliberately omits its own identity

limitations: The reviewer did not rerun or retime the 150 services; a new run would create new optimizer and timing observations.
The reviewer verified every frozen record and source digest and recomputed the main comparisons, but did not independently re-prove every inherited theorem.
Single-run service clocks are treated as descriptive and support no hardware-general performance inference.
No claim is made that spline or ridge dominates outside the declared R42 scalar and coupled economies.
This advisory review is not an Econometric Society editorial decision.
